title: Eye exam for diabetes
what: An eye doctor checks the retina through a widened pupil. This finds changes from diabetes early, while they can still be stopped.
why: For people with diabetes, usually once a year, more often if changes are already found.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes, including waiting for the drops; results right away
tell_doctor: Your type of diabetes and how long you have had it
Your latest HbA1c (long-term blood sugar) result
If you have high blood pressure
If you had laser treatment or eye injections

prepare.title: Food and medicines
prepare.text: Eat and take your medicines as usual.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: After the drops, it is hard to drive. It is better to have someone with you.

bring: Your glucose meter and a snack
steps: Your vision and eye pressure are checked
Drops are put in to widen your pupils
The doctor looks at the back of your eye with a lens
Sometimes a photo of the retina or an OCT scan is taken
feel: The light is bright during the exam
After the drops, close-up vision is blurry and light feels too bright for a few hours
after: Do not drive until the drops wear off
You get the result right away
Your next exam is as your doctor plans
Keeping your blood sugar and blood pressure under control protects your eyes
red_flags: A dark curtain or many floaters in front of the eye

faq.q: Why go if I see well?
faq.a: Changes in the retina are not felt for a long time. The exam finds them early.

faq.q: Can I keep my vision with diabetes?
faq.a: Yes. Controlling blood sugar and blood pressure and regular exams matter.

reminders.text: Eye exam tomorrow. Eat and take your medicines as usual. Better not to drive.
